title: Psalm 124:1–8
context: A Song of Ascents of David: corporate thanksgiving after narrow escape. If the LORD had not been on Israel's side when enemies rose, flood and snare would have finished them. Blessed be the LORD—help is in His name, Maker of heaven and earth. Pilgrim praise names deliverance as God's alone.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: What older interpreters in each camp said about the LORD on Israel's side, escape from flood and snare, and help in the Maker's name.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English editions of the sources named.

arminian.quote: If it had not been the Lord—If God had not, in a very especial manner, supported and defended us, we had all been swallowed up alive, and destroyed by a sudden destruction, so that not one would have been left. Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare—This is a fine image; and at once shows the weakness of the Jews, and the cunning of their adversaries. Humanly speaking there was no prospect of their escape: but the Lord was on their side. God thus broke the snare, and the bird escaped; while the poacher was caught in his own trap. Our help is in the name of the Lord—In open assaults, and in insidious attacks, we have no helper but God; and from him our deliverance must come.

reformed.quote: The Church having been providentially delivered from extreme peril, David exhorts true believers to thanksgiving, and teaches them by this memorable example, that their safety depends solely upon the grace and power of God. He affirms that the deliverance and the salvation of the people proceeded from nothing else than God's succor. He only truly attributes his deliverance to God, who acknowledges himself to have been lost before he was delivered. Our help is in the name of Jehovah: he not only gives thanks for one benefit, but affirms that the Church cannot continue safe except in so far as she is protected by the hand of God. His object is to animate the children of God with the assured hope that their life is in perfect safety under the divine guardianship. The name of God is nothing else than God himself; yet it implies that as he has disclosed to us his grace by his word, we have ready access to him.
reformed.source: Commentary on the Book of Psalms (on Psalm 124)

verses.text: If it had not been the LORD who was on our side, let Israel now say,
verses.arminianNotes:
If the LORD had not been on our side—let Israel say it aloud. Corporate memory opens with a conditional that drives thanksgiving, not idle speculation about what might have been.

Classical Arminians find a people invited to confess deliverance together. God truly sided with them in trouble; they freely join the refrain that keeps gratitude awake on every ascent.
verses.reformedNotes:
If the LORD had not been on our side—Israel must say so. The counterfactual exposes how completely safety hung on God's presence with His covenant people, not on their skill.

Being "on our side" is covenant initiative. The church's survival past rising foes is not a near-miss of luck but the LORD's prior commitment to those He claims as His own.
verses.keyContrast: Both urge Israel to confess that only the LORD's being "on our side" explains survival. Arminians press a welcomed siding with those who trust Him; Reformed interpreters stress God's covenant commitment that precedes and explains the people's escape.

verses.text: if it had not been the LORD who was on our side, when men rose up against us,
verses.arminianNotes:
Again: if the LORD had not been on our side, when men rose against us. Hostility is named plainly; God's siding is confessed as the decisive difference between ruin and pilgrimage.

When opposition rises, do not credit your own grit first. Join Israel's confession—His help met enemies, and warm thanksgiving should meet that help on the road.
verses.reformedNotes:
The LORD on our side, when men rose up. Human uprising meets divine allegiance; without that allegiance, the story of the people ends differently and darker.

People's rising does not surprise the covenant Lord. His being for His own is the reason the ascent continues past the threat instead of ending under it.

verses.text: then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us,
verses.arminianNotes:
Swallowed alive—anger kindled against us. The "then" paints how total the loss would have been without the LORD standing between Israel and kindled rage.

Arminian interpreters use this honesty pastorally: name how close ruin felt, then praise. Gratitude grows when the alternative is faced without minimizing either the danger or the mercy that intervened.
verses.reformedNotes:
Swallowed alive when anger kindled—the counterfactual is mercilessly clear. Apart from God, Israel's story is consumption by foes, not continued pilgrimage toward Zion.

The church learns its frailty by imagining life without God's restraint of wrathful enemies. Deliverance magnifies Him, not our near-escape skills or nerve.

verses.text: then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul.
verses.arminianNotes:
Flood and torrent would have swept and gone over us. Chaos imagery says the threat was overwhelming, not merely inconvenient or briefly alarming on the way.

Bring flood-memories to God in honest praise. He rescued; you did not swim the torrent alone. Let that truth reshape how you trust Him when the next surge rises.
verses.reformedNotes:
Flood swept away; torrent gone over—waters that drown the unprotected. Without the LORD, the people are debris in a current they cannot manage.

Providence includes holding back floods that would erase His people. The Ascents song refuses to treat survival as a self-navigated near miss.

verses.text: Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul.
verses.arminianNotes:
Raging waters over us—the third "then" finishes the dread picture. Total submersion was the alternative to God's help, and the psalm will not soften that fact.

Arminian readers urge lingering here long enough to feel the "almost," then move to blessing. Fear faced honestly fuels freer, warmer thanksgiving on the ascent.
verses.reformedNotes:
Raging waters would have gone over us. The stack of "thens" leaves no residual credit for Israel's strength, strategy, or luck under the flood.

The church's existence past such waters is grace upon grace. God alone stands between His people and the flood that would have closed over them forever.

verses.text: Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth.
verses.arminianNotes:
Blessed be the LORD—He has not given us as a prey to their teeth. Blessing answers the rescue with speech that honors Him rather than our escape artists.

Do not stop at relief; speak blessing aloud. Prey spared should become people who praise, freely ascribing the escape to the LORD's kindness and power.
verses.reformedNotes:
Blessed be the LORD who refused to give us as prey. Teeth were ready; God withheld the gift of His people to the predators who hungered for them.

Not being given as prey is God's decision before it is our relief. Blessing is the fitting response to a will that kept His own from the jaws.

verses.text: Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the fowler’s snare. The snare is broken, and we have escaped.
verses.arminianNotes:
Escaped like a bird; the snare is broken—and we have escaped! Freedom is celebrated twice so joy will not stay muted after such a trap.

Wesleyan Arminians hear invitation to rejoice in liberation. The broken snare calls for glad testimony on the road: God freed us; we walk on unbound and grateful.
verses.reformedNotes:
Bird from the fowlers' snare—snare broken, escape secured. Capture was certain until God snapped the trap that human skill could not open.

Escape is His breaking, not our clever twisting free. The doubled "escaped" underlines a deliverance wrought for the trapped, not achieved by them.

verses.text: Our help is in the LORD’s name, who made heaven and earth.
verses.arminianNotes:
Help is in the LORD’s name of the LORD—Maker of heaven and earth. Past escape becomes present confession for every remaining mile of the ascent.

Keep seeking help where creation's Lord invites trust. The name that rescued still receives pilgrim dependence with open welcome and aid.
verses.reformedNotes:
Our help is in the LORD's name, Maker of heaven and earth. Creator power and covenant name together ground the people's ongoing safety beyond one escape.

Help located in His name is not a technique but a confession of who He is. The Maker remains the only adequate help for His own forever.
verses.keyContrast: Both locate help in the LORD who made heaven and earth. Arminians typically underline continued, willing reliance on that name; Reformed commentators emphasize that help resides in God's name as the sure source for His people, not in creaturely alternatives.
